findings.body:
**Validate `durable_artifact_root` before returning it.**

In `src/ops/crq/backfillInventory.ts:183`, the type assertion does not validate the value. An otherwise valid configuration with `"durable_artifact_root": true` passes the prerequisite checks. Line 281 then passes a boolean to `effects.artifacts`, which requires a string.

Require a nonempty string before returning the settings. Keep valid string roots accepted.
findings.title: Validate `durableartifactroot` before returning it.
Reject duplicate keys in `parseCanonical`.

findings.body:
**Do not treat a truncated lookup as proof that no advisory exists.**

At `src/ops/crq/clientHealthRecord.ts:221`, `--limit 100` caps the returned issues. ([cli.github.com](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_help_reference?utm_source=openai)) If `opening=true`, `issue_number=null`, and the original advisory falls outside that result, Lines 227-237 clear the opening marker. Lines 242-260 then create a duplicate advisory.

Search for the advisory specifically. If the bounded lookup cannot establish absence, retain the unresolved opening marker instead of creating another issue. Preserve creation when a complete lookup finds no advisory.
findings.title: Do not treat a truncated lookup as proof that no advisory exists.

findings.body:
**Reject unsupported shell quoting before splitting the command.**

At Line 98, `CRQ_QUEUE_PRINCIPAL='dev CRQ_QUEUE_POLICY=/srv/crq/policy.json'` becomes two accepted assignments. The checker returns `ok:true`. The shell instead treats the quoted text as one principal value, so this command does not assign `CRQ_QUEUE_POLICY`. ([gnu.org](https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Single-Quotes.html?utm_source=openai))

Reject quotes and unsupported whitespace before splitting, or use shell-aware tokenization. Keep the supplied unquoted queue and author commands valid.
findings.title: Reject unsupported shell quoting before splitting the command.

findings.body:
**Validate the values of allowed options.**

A valid queue line with `expiry-time="not-a-date"` returns `ok:true`. Line 190 accepts the name, but no later branch checks its value. OpenSSH rejects this expiry value, so installing the approved line prevents authentication with that key. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openssh/openssh-portable/V_9_9_P2/auth-options.c))

Validate `expiry-time` syntax and the required quoted argument for `from`. Preserve valid optional settings.
findings.title: Validate the values of allowed options.

findings.body:
**Reject a second `command` option.**

For `restrict,command="false",command="<valid queue command>"`, Line 198 replaces the first command. The checker validates only the final command and returns `ok:true`. OpenSSH rejects multiple `command` clauses, so the approved key cannot authenticate. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openssh/openssh-portable/V_9_9_P2/auth-options.c))

Add a problem when `command` is already set. Keep a single valid command accepted.
findings.title: Reject a second `command` option.

findings.body:
**Reject malformed UTF-8 before rewriting the queue.**

At Line 333, the default decoder replaces invalid bytes rather than rejecting them. A literal `0xFF` inside `diagnostic` becomes U+FFFD. Reconciliation then sends the changed field to `writeQueue` at Line 682, even though publication does not own that field. Use fatal UTF-8 decoding so both queue write paths reject malformed bytes but still accept a valid, intentionally encoded U+FFFD. ([encoding.spec.whatwg.org](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/))
findings.title: Reject malformed UTF-8 before rewriting the queue.

findings.body:
**Read retained events once per reconciliation pass.**

Line 576 lists, reads and parses the entire retained outbox for each newly acknowledged item. A merge of 100 items against 10,000 retained records makes at least one million sequential file reads while holding `tick.lock`. Build the source-key index on the first lookup in each merge and add newly spooled events to it. Rebuild it on retry so records retained before a failed queue write remain reusable.
findings.title: Read retained events once per reconciliation pass.

findings.body:
**Implement the required JSON output protocol.**

In `src/ops/crq/readOnlyStatus.ts`, Line 227 rejects `health --json` even when the queue is valid. Line 515 then returns empty stdout and narration on stderr. The supplied `runStatusCli` forwards this result unchanged. Operational failures at Line 250 also omit the JSON artifact.

Accept `--json` and return one JSON artifact for usage and operational failures. Keep stderr empty in machine mode. Also move plain-text help away from stdout or encode it as JSON.

As per coding guidelines, “Every operation invocation writes machine-readable JSON to stdout” and “In machine mode (`--json`) stderr stays empty.”







Also applies to: 250-250, 515-515
findings.title: Implement the required JSON output protocol.

findings.body:
**Request publication after spooling a new quarantine event.**

With a configured rollout, `oversizeQuarantine` spools the replacement event and returns `publication: "spooled"` without calling `requestPublication`. The early return at Line 759 bypasses the signal used for ordinary records at Line 769. After `spoolEvent` succeeds, request publication when `configured` is true. Keep the no-rollout path unchanged.
findings.title: Request publication after spooling a new quarantine event.

findings.body:
**Skip receipt preloading for explicit repeats.**

An explicit repeat reads and parses every distinct retained local-review receipt while `tick.lock` is held. `admit` never calls `verifyReceipt` when `repeat` is true, so these reads delay other queue writes without affecting admission. Skip `retainedReceiptIds` for explicit repeats and keep verification on the non-repeat path.
findings.title: Skip receipt preloading for explicit repeats.

findings.body:
**Correct the `installSnapshot` contract comment to version 1.**

The `installSnapshot` contract at `src/ops/crq/reviewCapability.ts:113` says it installs a version-2 snapshot. The submit wire schema and the production installer both accept only version 1, so the comment misstates the required version. A maintainer who follows it could build a version-2 snapshot, which `WireSchema` rejects before the request reaches this effect.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-  /** Install a version-2 snapshot into the repository clone, bound to the commit. */
+  /** Install a version-1 snapshot into the repository clone, bound to the commit. */
```

</details>
findings.title: Correct the `installSnapshot` contract comment to version 1.

findings.body:
**Re-issue the publication signal when a retry matches a pending record.**

A retry of a record whose spool succeeded but whose `requestPublication` failed returns `duplicate` with no events. The publication block at `src/ops/crq/reviewCapability.ts:727-771` runs only when `imported.events` is non-empty, so `requestPublication` is not called again. The event stays in the pending outbox. It reaches the publisher only on a later publisher run. No second event is created, and no event is lost.

When the retry matches a pending record, the publication request must be issued again. The response must not report `publication: 'disabled'` while the rollout is enabled. The fix choice is open. Re-signal on the duplicate path, or make the spool and signal one retryable step. Either option must end with a publication request for the still-pending event.
findings.title: Re-issue the publication signal when a retry matches a pending record.

findings.body:
**Reject or honor explicit float `index` values in result requests.**

An explicit `index` written as `1.0` or `1e0` is accepted by the wire schema but ignored by the result handler. The handler then returns chunk 0 even when the caller asks for chunk 1. The handler reads the index only when the parsed token has the `int` kind (`src/ops/crq/reviewCapability.ts:453`). Float tokens do not have that kind, so the code falls back to `0`.

Make each explicit `index` token either select the requested chunk or fail as a validation error. An omitted `index` must still select chunk 0. Integer tokens such as `1` already select the requested chunk.
findings.title: Reject or honor explicit float `index` values in result requests.
